questions.question: What is secondary data? Elaborate the sources of secondary data along with / its merits and demerits.
questions.solution_html:
• Secondary data refers to data that has already been collected, processed
  • and published by someone else for a purpose different from the current
  • research. Instead of gathering fresh (primary) data, researchers use
  • existing information available in reports, publications, or databases.
  • Secondary data can be broadly classified into published and unpublished
  • sources
  • Published Sources
  • o Government Publications: Census reports, Economic Surveys
  • Statistical Abstracts, reports from ministries and departments.
  • o International Organizations: Reports from organizations like World
  • Bank, International Monetary Fund, United Nations.
  • o Research Institutions and Universities: Academic journals, working
  • papers, theses, and dissertations.
  • o Books, Journals, Newspapers, and Magazines: Provide qualitative
  • and quantitative information.
  • o Websites and Online Databases: Government portals, company
  • websites, and digital archives.

  • number of elements. The total number of units is limited and known

questions.question: What is secondary data? Elaborate the sources of secondary data along with / its merits and demerits.
questions.solution_html:
• Secondary data refers to data that has already been collected, processed
  • and published by someone else for a purpose different from the current
  • research. Instead of gathering fresh (primary) data, researchers use
  • existing information available in reports, publications, or databases.
  • Secondary data can be broadly classified into published and unpublished
  • sources
  • Published Sources
  • o Government Publications: Census reports, Economic Surveys
  • Statistical Abstracts, reports from ministries and departments.
  • o International Organizations: Reports from organizations like World
  • Bank, International Monetary Fund, United Nations.
  • o Research Institutions and Universities: Academic journals, working
  • papers, theses, and dissertations.
  • o Books, Journals, Newspapers, and Magazines: Provide qualitative
  • and quantitative information.
  • o Websites and Online Databases: Government portals, company
  • websites, and digital archives.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Establish the meaning of Probability sampling and explain the major probability / sampling methods.
questions.solution_html:
• Probability sampling is a sampling technique in which every unit of the
  • population has a known and non-zero chance of being selected.
  • Selection is done using random methods, ensuring that the sample is
  • representative and free from personal bias. It is widely used in scientific
  • and statistical research because it allows valid generalizations about the
  • population.
  • Major Probability Sampling Methods
